text:
natalie_ops: Hey — deployed a service under systemd and started seeing 401 invalid_api_key from the hosted API. Same key works from my laptop curl. Anyone seen this after a systemd deploy?

sam_support: Can you paste the systemd unit (trimmed) and the exact curl that succeeds locally? also which env var name you set?

natalie_ops: Sure — unit snippet below (redacted):

```ini
[Unit]
Description=example worker
After=network.target

[Service]
Environment=REDWOOD_API_KEY="sk_live_ABC123def=="
ExecStart=/usr/bin/node /opt/app/index.js
Restart=on-failure

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
```

Local curl that works:
```bash
curl -H "Authorization: ApiKey sk_live_ABC123def==" https://api.redwood.example/v1/chat -d '{"input":"hi"}'
```

When I run the same curl on the server outside systemd it works, but requests from the running service get 401.

sam_support: when you `env | grep REDWOOD` on the server (outside of systemd) what do you see? and can you paste the request headers your app sends when running under systemd?

natalie_ops: `env | grep REDWOOD` shows: `REDWOOD_API_KEY="sk_live_ABC123def=="` (including the quotes). I dumped the outgoing header from the app logs and got: `Authorization: ApiKey "sk_live_ABC123def=="` which looks wrong.

deploy-bot: deployed example-worker v2026.03.15-41 by natalie_ops :rocket:

emma_engineer: Ah yep — systemd Environment= does not strip quotes the way a shell does. If you write `Environment=VAR="value"` the literal quotes become part of the env value. That means your app is sending a header with embedded double-quotes and our auth layer treats that as a different token -> 401 (we canonicalize/exact-match API keys).

Suggested fixes:
- Edit the unit and remove the quotes: `Environment=REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk_live_ABC123def==`
- Or put the secret in an EnvironmentFile and reference it: `EnvironmentFile=/etc/default/example-worker` (no quotes inside the file either).
- After changing: `systemctl daemon-reload && systemctl restart example-worker`

Quick repro you can run on the server to see the problem:
```bash
# shows the quotes are in the env value
printf '%s' "$REDWOOD_API_KEY" | sed -n l
# will print: \"sk_live_ABC123def==\"
```

sam_support: thanks for the root cause. once you restart with the corrected unit can you confirm the app logs show `Authorization: ApiKey sk_live_ABC123def==` (no quotes) and that calls succeed?

natalie_ops: Yep — removed the quotes, restarted, logs now show header without quotes and the endpoint returns 200. 🎉 Thanks both.

emma_engineer: Nice. I'll add a short note to our troubleshooting KB about systemd quoting gotchas and 401s. :memo:

sam_support: Marking as resolved, closing thread. :white_check_mark:
